The formats cover different motivations rather than five exclusive audience segments. Each contributes a distinct kind of satisfaction. A common daily home and shared Mashal connect the choices. This is the reason for the starting mix of five, not evidence that five is the optimum or that cross-game conversion is proven. Sources: supplied design rationale and organizer brief pp. 9, 13–17.

Shabd demonstrates the authored answer अनुसंधान with a space explainer, meaning and a related article. Jodi uses sourced mission/achievement relationships in a labelled archive pack. The current standalone prototypes share a daily home/edition and common Hindi help and result conventions. The implemented Mashal ledger joins completions across all five games. Each game can count at most once per calendar date. Five new daily game completions earn a level, either different games today or the same game on five dates. Switching demo editions, replays, practice and restored results do not add extra bars. The earned level persists in this browser when storage is available; the consecutive-day streak is separate and gaps do not erase levels. Round/result history is current-visit only. Article return preserves the current round/result within the visit. Readers need not finish all five. Sources: current Doc/Mashal journey.md, src/core/mashal-progress.js, src/systems/progression.js and prototype article return behavior.

These are engagement hypotheses, not measured return rates. Today offers a complete payoff through solving, understanding or expression. The intended daily publishing rhythm supplies another invitation. Mastery and the persistent shared Mashal offer depth over time. Current editions are authored demos; checked editorial publishing, random validated Carrom level generation and hosted share invitations are future work. Personal round/history storage lasts only the current visit. Assess voluntary return, useful article engagement and editorial effort in a reader pilot. Source: supplied Bhaskar Daily Games Design Rationale.docx, output/design-rationale, 12 October 2026. Proposed benefits and repeat reasons are product hypotheses, not measured retention or comprehension outcomes.
Closing: ordinary habits gave us the starting points. One daily destination gives those interests a short, approachable moment of participation. Reporting supplies context and meaning where useful. Niti can carry a thought into a conversation, while Nishana offers familiar skill play. The five choices form one submission concept. The benefits should earn validation with readers. A brief prototype demonstration can follow this close.
